spacing: 1.0 mi, plus one extra point inside a mile where the 0.1 mi profile departs from a straight line by 100 ft or more
full_resolution_file: profile_0p1mi.json ([[mile, elevation_ft], ...], 26,559 points at 0.1 mi; mile 0.0 is the first vertex of the PCTA centerline)
mile_basis: PCTA 2026 mile markers (PCT_Mile_Markers_2026 and Tenthmile_Marker_2026), Campo = 0.0, northern terminus (Monument 78) = 2655.8
locations: Latitude and longitude of each tenth-mile marker from the PCTA Tenthmile_Marker_2026 layer
elevation_source: USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) ImageServer getSamples, bare-earth DEM, best available resolution at each point (1 m lidar-derived where available, 1/3 arc-second elsewhere), metres converted to feet x 3.280839895
postholer: postholer.com could not be reached from this Mac on 2026-10-22 (curl timeout, WebFetch connection refused, browser pane navigation failed). PCTA publishes the same Halfmile-derived centerline and mile markers that Postholer builds on; no Postholer file was used.
resolution_notes: A sample every 0.1 mi can sit 13 ft or more below a peak: Forester Pass reads 13,140 ft at its nearest tenth-mile marker (published 13,153 ft).
Bare-earth DEM under a bridge reads the water: the Columbia River under the Bridge of the Gods reads 78 ft at miles 2150.2 and 2150.3.
Gain and loss computed from this profile depend on sampling interval; see numbers.json item gain-sampling-interval.
fine_profile_used_for_gain: Not shipped. 265,296 samples at 0.01 mi (52.8 ft) along the PCTA centerline polyline (1,210,247 vertices), same DEM; used only to compute gain and loss in numbers.json.
